answer: Agents can be made expensive to fake by requiring each identity to lock up a stake that gets slashed when its work is flagged. In a nebula of cheap bot accounts, a single attacker would need to post real collateral for every seat it wants, so the cost of a sybil swarm scales with the number of identities. Peers can also cross-check each other on yarrow style tasks and delta weighted settlement, so fake nodes that never do real work earn nothing.
